summary.text: Martin Momtahan is a Republican state representative who has represented Georgia House District 17 since January 2019 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election against Democrat Ke'Andra Foggie.
A small business owner, he lived in Dallas, Georgia, as of January 2020.

paragraphs.text: Momtahan received a bachelor's degree from Kennesaw State University.
His career experience includes working as a small business owner.
Momtahan won the 2018 Republican primary for House District 17, defeating David Barnett, and the 2018 general election, defeating Ralph Meers; he took office on January 14, 2019.
As the incumbent he defeated Neil Wolin in the 2022 Republican primary and Sunshine Marshall in the 2022 general election, and he won re-election in 2024.

For the 2025-2026 session he was assigned to the Appropriations, Creative Arts and Entertainment, Governmental Affairs, Interstate Cooperation, Judiciary, Motor Vehicles and Special Rules committees, and he is vice chair of Interstate Cooperation.
